evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository and InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository; they are storage-only adapters with no business rules

src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: OrderController is constructor-injected with OrderService and CatalogueService, and its routes call only orders.place/list/advance/cancel and catalogue.add/list
src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: error mapping is kept in the single private helper handle() and id checking in orderId()
src/infrastructure/server.ts: createApp() is the only place that builds the repositories, services and controller and connects them

src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: const states: readonly OrderState[] = ["placed", ...] re-lists the domain's OrderState values; this is only a concern if the domain already exports a runtime list (not visible)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files cover one concern: the infrastructure adapters plus the composition root. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the persistence adapters that implement the domain repository ports. order-controller.ts is the HTTP adapter and delegates only to the application services. server.ts is the single place where objects are built and connected. No file bypasses the module's abstractions: the controller never touches repositories, and only createApp wires dependencies. Error mapping (handle) and order id checking (orderId) each live in one place. Lower-confidence concern: order-controller.ts re-lists the OrderState values in a runtime array (states / isState). If src/domain/order.ts already exports such a list, that would be a duplicated invariant. That file isn't in the material, and checking input at the boundary against a type-only union is a common pattern, so it isn't reported as a violation. OrderController also serves /products through CatalogueService. The name is narrow, but it remains one cohesive HTTP adapter.
